history.new: Full-period tables are Klimov's finite UFS-groupoids with periodic universal Fibonacci sequence (P. Klimov, 'Universal Fibonacci sequences and UFS-groupoids', arXiv:2604.05754, 2026, Thm 4.2: their cycles are the de Bruijn sequences B(n,2)). Klimov characterises them through distance-1 pairs only and leaves open whether one can be a quasigroup (Problem 7.5). The distance-2 characterisation was not found. Tuscan-2 squares (Etzion-Golomb-Taylor 1989) and recursive MDS codes are different objects. Small (Historian audit 2026-10-19, reviews/historian_C11_C20.md).

statement:
A full-period table is a quasigroup iff in its cycle x_0 ... x_{n^2-1} every ordered pair also occurs exactly once
as (x_i, x_{i+2}); equivalently the windows (x_{i-1}, x_i, x_{i+1}) run once through the n^2 triples
(a, b, b*a) of the Latin square (a universal cycle of the quasigroup).
title: Full-period quasigroups are cycles in which every pair occurs once at distance 1 and once at distance 2
